content:
If you open Apple Maps today, you will notice that Apple has begun renaming Lake Ontario to "Lake of the Americas." This rename follows an executive order by Trump last week, and is part of his ongoing trade dispute with Canada.

This change was first spotted by Bloomberg, and applies to Apple Maps users in the United States. Canadian Apple Maps users will still see the name "Lake Ontario." Apple Maps users in other regions will see both names displayed together.

Google Maps had earlier renamed Lake Ontario to Lake of the Americas. At the time, Google said its policy is to adopt names designated by the U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS).

U.S. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said yesterday that Trump had "directly contacted Apple" to request the change. It appears that conversation prompted Apple to follow suit and update the name on Apple Maps.

Meanwhile, MapQuest announced last Thursday that it would refuse to rename Lake Ontario to Lake of the Americas, and that decision caused its downloads to surge.

The change appears to be rolling out gradually to Apple Maps users. My own iPhone still shows Lake Ontario, but some of my colleagues at 9to5Mac have already seen Lake of the Americas.

Last year, when Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico to be renamed the "Gulf of America," Apple made the same change on Apple Maps.
